scope: R2/SCAN-CORE-01: same-installation entrypoints with conflicting versions
status: implemented-and-isolated-verified; real host scan not performed

reviewFindings.entryVersionMismatch: gap: one installation kept a single record and silently dropped a second launcher whose probe reported a different version
reviewFindings.nonExecutablePathEntry: covered: find_executable only accepts an existing file with an allowed extension, and a launcher that cannot start maps to StartFailed with the error text
reviewFindings.permissionDeniedDirectory: covered: PermissionDenied is produced both for a spawn failure and for exit code 5 or an access-denied message, and has a dedicated fixture

implementation: ExternalEnv gains version_conflicts: the launchers of the same installation whose reported version differs from the selected record
each duplicate launcher is now probed instead of being dropped unexamined
a conflict records the launcher path plus either its version or the probe error
conflicts are collected per selected row so they survive the per-batch dedup
scan_discovered adds one warning per affected tool naming up to three conflicting entrypoints and the total count
the report status becomes Partial when any such conflict exists, so the scan is not presented as fully consistent
version_conflicts is empty for identical versions and for the pip-module row

ui.command: node tests/run-ui.mjs <global playwright module> tests/settings-ui.mjs tests/startup-ui.mjs tests/release-052-ui.mjs tests/download-ui.mjs tests/package-manager-update-ui.mjs tests/scans-ui.mjs tests/scan-ui.mjs tests/sizes-ui.mjs tests/packages-ui.mjs

notVerified: No real host installation with genuinely divergent launcher versions was scanned
The UI does not yet render version_conflicts; only the warning text surfaces them
limitations: A conflict is recorded only for launchers sharing the same resolved install identity; separate installs remain separate rows
Both probes run, so a scan costs one extra process per duplicate launcher
A launcher whose probe fails is counted as a conflict rather than an installation failure
